blocks.html: 🦒 What to Expect
The interview process can vary widely from opportunity to opportunity, but almost all take place over a combination of the following 3 stages.

Instead of having 3 distinct Stages, some studios will carry out Stage 1, then hybridise Stages 2+3 into a single phase.
Entry-level positions will generally be subject to a lighter-intensity ‘combined’ process than those typically used for more senior applicants.

You can find some common Questions & Answers to have ready for each interview stage at:
‣
Stage 1: The Pre-Screen
Duration: ~20-40min
Great! Your CV and Portfolio have been noticed, and you have been invited for your first in-person contact with the compay you are potentially looking to join.
This first stage will typically be an introductory phone or video call with a Recruiter or a member of HR at the company.

The goal of this interview is to mostly establish a first connection, for them to get to know more about you, your experience, and your ambitions at a surface level, and for you to get to know less widely-available information about the studio, role, and project you could be joining.

Typically, no discipline specifics or technical conversation will be discussed. However, if both parties are willing to, salary expectations could be a touch-point to ensure there is a match between your expecations, and the salary-band for the opening.
Stage 2: Interview with the Hiring Manager(s)
Duration: ~60-90min
If you pass the pre-screen, your next interview will most likely be a video call, or on-site interview with the Hiring Manager for the position, as well as was 1-2 chosen members of their entourage.

It is during this stage that you will get into the nitty-gritty of your craft, and most importantly, this will be your chance to ask a lot of questions about their methods of development and full expectations of the role.

If the studio in question requires tests to be completed as part of their hiring process, if there is interest to proceed further, it is most likely at the conclusion of this stage that you will be asked if you are willing to perform a 'Take-Home Test' as a precursor to Stage 3.
You can find more information on UI Tests at ‣.
Stage 3: Meeting the Team
Duration: 2-4hrs
First of all. Congratulations if you've made it this far. This typically means that the results of the test you performed met, or exceeded expectations.
This stage will in most cases involve a quarter, to a half-day on-site, in which you will get to meet the wider team over different sessions, for their appraisal.

If you are applying to a company outside of your immediate geographic region, it is customary for the company to cover your travel and accomodation costs.
If they do not mention this at the time of invitation, you should enquire before commiting.

If you were asked to perform a test, it is during a couple of these sessions that you will get the chance to talk about what you made, and to delve into the thinking and process behind what you created, as well as how you might potentially change or expand the results if given further information or constraints (This might be considered one form of an 'On-Site' Test.)
You can find more information on UI Tests at ‣.
In most cases, this time will generally be used as a 'chemistry fit' evaluation and for both you and them to see if you are the type of people who would get along, and work well together.
On your end, this is a great opportunity to find out more perspectives about the project, the company, and their processes.
In certain circumstances, you may be presented an offer at the end of this stage.
Good luck!
💃 Interview Dress Code.
Video game industry dress codes can initially appear disorderly compared to other workplaces, however, certain rules still apply.
General Guidelines.
Avoid wearing any of the following to an interview:

Do not follow your mother's advice to show up to your interview in any type of formal wear.
It won't make a bad impression per se, but it will almost certainly result in an awkward situation as it is considered extremely over-dressed for the industry.
Do <u>not</u> wear any athletic wear.
Do <u>not</u> wear any items of clothing with overly strong graphical elements (you can wear your favourite video game or sports team shirt after you're hired).
The following are recommended, provided they are well-fitting, and in good condition:
For shoes, pretty much anything from the 'casual footwear' category and above.
For lower body, you can't go wrong with your best pair of fitted jeans, chinos, or a casual skirt.
For your upper body; a button-up shirt, plain t-shirt, sweater, blouse, or a blazer are all good options.
